intro: Maryland runs its elections through the State Board of Elections and a local board of elections in each county and in Baltimore City.

id_rule.text: Most Maryland voters do not need to show ID. Some first-time voters are asked to show a photo ID, or a recent utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck or other government document with their name and address. If you register or update your address during early voting or on Election Day, bring a document that proves where you live.

elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register online or by mail
dates.detail: Mailed forms must be postmarked by this date. If you miss it, you can still register and vote on the same day at an early voting center in your county or on Election Day. Bring a document that proves where you live.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Vote at any early voting center in your county of residence, 7 am to 8 pm every day, including the weekend. You do not need an appointment.

dates.label: Deadline to request a mail-in ballot sent to you
dates.detail: Your request must be received, not just mailed, by this date, whether you send it online, by mail, or by fax. Maryland calls absentee voting "mail-in voting."

dates.label: Deadline to request a mail-in ballot online by email
dates.detail: This is the last day to request a ballot online that you get by email and print yourself. You can also request a ballot in person at your local board of elections until 8 pm on Election Day.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm, and same-day registration is available. A mail-in ballot must be postmarked by Nov. 3, or put in an official drop box or handed to your local board by 8 pm.
